summary.text:
Read on the covering Finance Report (2025/26 Financial Outturn) to Cabinet on 30 June 2026. Treasury is a single paragraph in §4.7 on page 3: borrowing £336.971m at an average 4.86%, investments £21m at 3.68%, at end of March 2026. There is no CFR, no maturity table, no prudential indicators, no split of debt by lender type, no MRP policy line and no discount or break-cost position. The seven appendices cover revenue, schools, reserves and capital — none is a treasury appendix. Detailed treasury reporting sits in a separate Annual Treasury Report to the Governance and Audit Committee that we do not yet hold.

Our PWLB price book carries 73 live loans totalling £249,329,261 at a weighted 4.3196% on 31 March 2026, against Denbighshire's published £336.971m all-in borrowing at 4.86% on the same date. That leaves £87.642m of non-PWLB debt at an implied ~6.40% weighted rate — LOBOs, Welsh Government loans, market debt or some mix. The paper does not itemise it. The £87.6m gap is a genuine future hook once the split is confirmed by their next Annual Treasury Report or a later Statement of Accounts (the one we hold is 2022/23, three years behind and pre-dates the current book).

The balance-sheet identity (CFR − external borrowing − other long-term liabilities = internal borrowing) cannot be tested from this paper — none of those lines is printed. Capital outturn (Appendix 7) shows £27.5m of prudential borrowing drawn in 2025/26, £21.4m of it against coastal defences with 85% funded by Welsh Government through the RSG, but the paper is silent on how and when it was drawn.

No email drafted. This is a covering report by the standard set in EMAIL_TEMPLATE.md §7: one treasury sentence, in a Cabinet paper about revenue, capital and reserves, with no treasury appendix to lean on and no forward finance meeting that would make this the right paper to write about. The right output is a thin note recording exactly that. Watch the GAC forward plan for the Annual Treasury Report — that is when this council becomes writable.
